MATERIAL_CORRECTION_TO_THE_STATED_PREMIS.what_was_measured: It does NOT. The helper passes a SINGLE endpoint. `git diff --name-only <commit>` compares that commit against the WORKING TREE (index and worktree), not against HEAD.
MATERIAL_CORRECTION_TO_THE_STATED_PREMIS.independent_proof: Reproduced in a disposable throwaway repository, not argued from documentation: with base B, one commit on top adding f2, and a staged-but-unshipped f3, `git diff --name-only B` returned [f2, f3] while `git diff --name-only B HEAD` returned [f2]. The one-endpoint form admits working-tree state; the two-endpoint form does not.
MATERIAL_CORRECTION_TO_THE_STATED_PREMIS.why_this_correction_is_load_bearing_and_: CLAUDE.md section 9 records this exact Windows/git hazard as MEASURED: `git diff <ref> -- <path>` semantics have previously diffed against the working tree unexpectedly, and the two-endpoint form must be verified. A correction lane that merely substituted a constant for the literal `HEAD` would find no `HEAD` to substitute, and a correction lane that added a second endpoint without understanding WHICH endpoint was mutable could rebind the wrong one. The mutable endpoint here is the WORKING TREE, and the fixed endpoint is already correct.
MATERIAL_CORRECTION_TO_THE_STATED_PREMIS.does_it_change_the_adjudication: No. It sharpens it. Both HEAD and the working tree are mutable objects; the defect class -- a historical control bound to a mutable endpoint -- is identical. Only the mechanics of the authorized correction change, and SECTION_B6 states them against the MEASURED form.

SECTION_B2_ORIGINAL_CANARY_SEMANTICS.what_the_canary_was_correct_to_do_at_aut: At the implementing lane, the worktree was the slice under construction and nothing else existed in it. base-vs-worktree was then a FAITHFUL measurement of the governed predicate, and the untracked arm was load-bearing: a newly authored file not yet added is exactly the way a lane accidentally exceeds its surface without git noticing. The control was not sloppy. It was correct for a lifecycle stage that has now ended.

SECTION_B3_WHY_IT_BECOMES_STALE.the_governed_predicate: The parent authority FUTURE_RUNTIME_WRITE_SURFACE states the rule as a property of a LANE and a SLICE: 'This is a CLOSED enumeration. A future implementation lane that needs a path not listed here has exceeded the slice and must STOP_FOR_AUTHORITY_DELTA rather than widen it silently.' NEW_ODS_REQUIRED.reversal_condition states it as 'if a future measurement finds the slice REQUIRES any protected path'. FIBIU19_DISJOINTNESS.re_derivation_obligation states it as 'An implementing lane re-derives it against its own base BEFORE COMMITTING'.
SECTION_B3_WHY_IT_BECOMES_STALE.what_the_predicate_quantifies_over: The slice's own authored diff. Every wording is about what the lane NEEDS, REQUIRES or AUTHORS -- never about every file that will ever be present in the branch's history.
SECTION_B3_WHY_IT_BECOMES_STALE.the_defect: After independent certification, the slice stopped being a thing under construction and became an immutable historical object. The helper's endpoints did not. From the first integration sync onward, base-vs-worktree stops answering 'what did this slice author?' and starts answering 'what does this branch differ by, from a base that is now several merges behind?' -- a different question, whose answer necessarily grows without bound as integration advances.
SECTION_B3_WHY_IT_BECOMES_STALE.the_falsity_it_produces: It causes the suite to assert that the FIBDB-053 runtime slice authored docs/ops/ods/ODS_V1_MAINTENANCE_ADDENDUM_v1.0.38.json. That is FALSE. That file was authored by the ODS v1.0.38 lane and merged through PR #199. Attributing it to the runtime slice is not a conservative over-reading; it is a factually wrong provenance claim that a governed control is asserting under its own authority.
SECTION_B3_WHY_IT_BECOMES_STALE.the_asymmetry_that_makes_it_unsafe_rathe: A control that reddens on inherited content is not fail-closed in any useful direction. It creates standing pressure to widen `authorised` to make a green appear -- and widening it would import integration content into the runtime slice's authority. The defect's natural remedy is the very act the closed-world contract forbids. That is why it is adjudicated here instead of being worked around.

SECTION_B4_BINDING_ADJUDICATION.status: FROZEN_BY_THIS_AMENDMENT. Phase 2 did not disprove the interpretation; the parent's own wording corroborates it.

A_the_governed_object.rule: The governed runtime slice is the object that was independently certified. It is identified by three immutable anchors and by nothing else.

B_the_measurement_endpoint.rule: The persistent historical canary for that slice MUST measure the immutable certified object: `git diff --name-only <CERTIFICATION_BASE> <CERTIFIED_CANDIDATE>` -- the TWO-ENDPOINT form, with both endpoints fixed commit identifiers.
B_the_measurement_endpoint.explicitly_not: NOT the mutable branch HEAD, and NOT the working tree, which per SECTION_B2 is what the original one-endpoint form actually read.
B_the_measurement_endpoint.why_two_endpoints_is_stated_as_a_require: Because the original defect is precisely that one endpoint was left implicit and therefore mutable. A correction that names only the far endpoint and leaves the near one implicit would reproduce the defect in a new spelling.

SECTION_B4_BINDING_ADJUDICATION.C_no_surface_widening: Inherited integration paths are NOT added to FUTURE_RUNTIME_WRITE_SURFACE. That enumeration remains CLOSED and remains exactly the paths the parent authority derived.
SECTION_B4_BINDING_ADJUDICATION.D_no_N_RC_08_exception: Inherited integration paths are NOT exceptions to N-RC-08. No protected-path rule is relaxed, narrowed, conditioned or given a carve-out by this amendment.

E_they_are_outside_the_slice_entirely.statement: An inherited integration path is not an authorized member of the slice and not an exception to a rule about the slice. It is not a member of the domain the slice's controls quantify over.
E_they_are_outside_the_slice_entirely.why_this_framing_and_not_an_exception_li: An exception list is a widening with extra steps: it concedes that the path is inside the domain and then excuses it, which means the next inherited path needs another excuse and the list grows with integration. Placing the paths outside the domain is the only formulation that does not grow.

F_where_integration_correctness_is_gover.statement: The post-certification sync is certified SEPARATELY, by comparing the synchronized PR head against its integration parent -- not by the slice's historical canary.
F_where_integration_correctness_is_gover.why_this_is_not_a_gap: The two questions are different and each keeps a control. 'Did the slice author only its authorized surface?' is answered forever by the immutable historical canary. 'Did this sync inherit integration faithfully and author nothing extra?' is answered by the sync evidence in SECTION_B9 and the focused recert in SECTION_B10. Nothing that was proven stops being proven; the proofs are simply asked of the object each one is actually about.

classification.this_is: A LIFECYCLE CLARIFICATION. It rebinds one measurement endpoint to the object the governed predicate was always about.
classification.this_is_not: A SURFACE WIDENING. Zero paths are added to any authorised enumeration. The closed 13-path surface is byte-identical before and after. No control is removed, suppressed, weakened or made conditional.
classification.falsifiable_statement_of_the_distinction: After the authorized correction, the set of paths the exact-write-set control accepts is UNCHANGED (13). Only the set of paths it is shown is changed -- from 'whatever the branch currently differs by' to 'what the certified slice authored'. A reviewer can verify this claim by diffing the `authorised` array before and after and finding it identical.

SECTION_B5_UNSAFE_ALTERNATIVES_REJECTED.rule: This STOP may NOT be resolved by any of the following. Each is PROHIBITED by this amendment, and a lane that proposes one has misread the adjudication rather than found a shortcut.

prohibited.alternative: Adding the five currently-inherited ODS/scripts/tests paths to the `authorised` enumeration.
prohibited.why_prohibited: It converts integration-authored content into runtime-slice authority. It is also self-defeating: the five are the five inherited AT THIS BASE. The next integration commit produces a different five, so the list would have to be re-widened at every sync, and the enumeration would stop being closed in any meaningful sense.

prohibited.alternative: Filtering a path merely because it came from integration.
prohibited.why_prohibited: 'Came from integration' is a claim about provenance that the filter would have to trust rather than prove. A slice path that was ALSO touched by integration would be silently exonerated, which is exactly the overlap case the closed-world contract exists to catch.
It is a protected-path relaxation wearing the costume of a scoping fix. N-RC-08's whole content is that this prefix is refused.

prohibited.alternative: Changing the protected-path rules or the protected-prefix list.
prohibited.why_prohibited: The defect is in WHAT the control is shown, not in WHAT it refuses. Editing the refusal to accommodate a bad input is weakening a gate to obtain a PASS, forbidden by CLAUDE.md section 5.
Same. A skipped control is a removed control with a comment.

prohibited.alternative: Making changedPaths ignore arbitrary unfamiliar paths.
prohibited.why_prohibited: It inverts the closed world into an open one. The control's entire strength is that an UNRECOGNISED path is a failure; a filter that drops unrecognised paths cannot ever fail, which is vacuity, not a fix.

prohibited.alternative: Asserting that a clean merge-tree, zero path overlap or a green CI proves authority.
prohibited.why_prohibited: Mechanical cleanliness is evidence about a merge, never a grant. This lane MEASURED a perfectly clean pure union -- 13/13 and 5/5 identical blobs, zero overlap, no conflict -- and that cleanliness is precisely what did NOT resolve the authority question. Treating it as if it had would be the 'it changed anyway' scope inference CLAUDE.md section 5 forbids.

SECTION_B5_UNSAFE_ALTERNATIVES_REJECTED.consolidated_reason: Every rejected alternative reaches green by making the runtime slice's authority absorb content it never authored, or by making a control unable to fail. The adjudication in SECTION_B4 reaches green by asking the control about the object it was always about. Only the latter leaves the closed-world contract intact.

SECTION_B7_UNTRACKED_FILE_DISPOSITION.the_question: The certified helper unions `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard` into changedPaths(). Once the tracked endpoints become immutable commits, what happens to that arm?
SECTION_B7_UNTRACKED_FILE_DISPOSITION.why_it_cannot_simply_be_kept: An untracked file in some future worktree is definitionally NOT part of commit b1d26b26. Unioning present-tense worktree state into a measurement of an immutable historical object reintroduces exactly the mutable endpoint this amendment removes -- and would do so silently, since the tracked half would look correct.
SECTION_B7_UNTRACKED_FILE_DISPOSITION.why_it_cannot_simply_be_deleted: The arm has real content: it is how a lane that authors a new file and forgets to `git add` it is caught. Deleting it outright would remove a protection, which SECTION_B4's own classification forbids this correction from doing.

ADJUDICATION.historical_arm: The section 6 historical controls -- N-RC-05, N-RC-06, N-RC-08 and the exact-write-set control -- run over the IMMUTABLE two-endpoint tracked diff ONLY. No untracked union. Their subject is a commit, and a commit has no untracked files.
ADJUDICATION.present_tense_arm: Untracked-file detection is RETAINED as a SEPARATE, EXPLICITLY NAMED control whose stated subject is the CORRECTION LANE'S OWN WORKING TREE, not the certified slice. It must assert that the lane's own worktree introduces no untracked path outside the single-file authorized surface of SECTION_B6.
ADJUDICATION.why_split_rather_than_merged: The two arms answer different questions about different objects and now have different lifetimes. Merging them is what made the original helper unable to state which object it was measuring. Separating them makes each one's subject nameable, and therefore falsifiable.
ADJUDICATION.non_vacuity_obligation_on_the_present_te: It must be proven capable of going RED -- an assertion over a worktree that is clean in CI is otherwise green forever and proves nothing. The proof must exhibit the arm reddening on an introduced untracked path, and must assert SETUP=SUCCESS so that a setup failure producing zero paths cannot satisfy it vacuously.

SECTION_B8_REQUIRED_NON_VACUITY.binding_on: The future correction lane AND its independent recertifier. A correction that lands without these is NOT certifiable under this amendment.
SECTION_B8_REQUIRED_NON_VACUITY.anti_vacuity_rule_inherited: Restated from the v1.0.1 manifest amendment and binding here: a control must assert its comparands as FROZEN STRINGS and must not re-derive them from the subject using the subject's own transformation. A battery that re-expresses its subject's predicate proves only that the copy behaves like the copy.
SECTION_B8_REQUIRED_NON_VACUITY.mutation_harness_requirement: Each mutant must be driven against a module identity the transform cache has not already served. It is MEASURED in this repository that vi.resetModules() does not invalidate vite's transform, so an on-disk mutation re-imported under the SAME module id executes the ORIGINAL and the battery is vacuous. Each mutant therefore needs a fresh module id and a witness assertion exclusive to that mutant.

The five paths measured in SECTION_B1 are the five inherited at AS_OF_HEAD 4680ae9c ONLY, and integration will have advanced. M1 proves the new endpoint is the reason the suite is green -- that green was earned, not inherited from a control that stopped being able to fail. M2, M3 and M4 prove that every refusal the certified control performed, it still performs, on the rebound input. A correction landing M1 without M2..M4 would have proven only that it changed something.

SECTION_B9_SYNC_CONTRACT.sequencing: This authority delta is integrated FIRST. The integration SHA the retry merges is then derived FRESH at that time.

Perform EXACTLY ONE normal merge of the then-current integration into PR #197.
Contain NO manual conflict resolution. A conflict is a STOP, not a thing to resolve by hand -- hand resolution authors bytes that no authority granted.

topology_of_the_correction_commit.rule: The canary successor correction MAY be committed as a DISTINCT successor commit associated with the sync. It may equally precede it. What is forbidden is leaving the order implicit.
topology_of_the_correction_commit.obligation: The topology and ordering MUST be stated explicitly in the retry's own evidence and MUST be independently certified. A correction folded invisibly into a merge commit is indistinguishable from a manual conflict resolution, which the clause above prohibits.
topology_of_the_correction_commit.why_this_matters_more_than_it_looks: The correction edits a file that is also one of the certified 13. If it is authored inside the merge, a certifier cannot separate 'the merge preserved the certified blob' from 'the merge changed it', because both statements would be about the same commit.

SECTION_B11_POST_MERGE_DURABILITY.claim: Binding the historical section 6 canary to the immutable certified candidate is durable after the PR sync, after the PR merge, and after arbitrarily many later unrelated integration commits.
SECTION_B11_POST_MERGE_DURABILITY.why: Both endpoints are fixed commit identifiers. `git diff --name-only 89022a9b b1d26b26` returns the same 13 paths regardless of where HEAD is, what the working tree contains, how many merges have landed, or whether the branch still exists -- because both commits are immutable and remain reachable once merged. The measurement has no dependency on present state at all, so there is no present state whose change can perturb it.
SECTION_B11_POST_MERGE_DURABILITY.the_durability_statement: The historical canary keeps testing the HISTORICAL CERTIFIED SLICE OBJECT. Later integration correctness is governed by later merge and recert evidence -- SECTION_B9 and SECTION_B10 -- which measure the synchronized head against its integration parent, the endpoint pair that question is actually about.
SECTION_B11_POST_MERGE_DURABILITY.what_it_must_NOT_do: It must NOT continue redefining the old slice whenever HEAD changes. A historical control whose subject moves is not a historical control; it is a present-tense control with a misleading name, which is exactly the artifact this amendment exists to retire.

the_objection_answered.objection: Does a canary that can never see present state stop protecting anything?
the_objection_answered.answer: No, because it never protected present state. Its four controls assert properties of what the slice AUTHORED -- no FIBIU-19 path, no protected path, no Stage-A apply, nothing outside the closed surface. Those are properties of a finished object and they are either true of it or not, permanently. Present-state protection is a different job, held by the sync contract, the focused recert, the ODS classifier at each lane's own base, and the present-tense untracked arm of SECTION_B7. Every one of those survives this amendment untouched.
the_objection_answered.residual_risk_stated_rather_than_denied: A control bound to immutable anchors cannot detect a NEW defect introduced after certification. That is not a regression -- the certified control could not do so either, since it reddened indiscriminately on inherited content and would have drowned any real signal. But it means the historical canary must never be cited as evidence about a present head, and SECTION_B10 item 5 exists so that the present head has its own 13-path control.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The mission premise that changedPaths() computes `git diff --name-only 89022a9b HEAD` is FALSE. The certified helper passes one endpoint and therefore compares the base against the WORKING TREE.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: The adjudication is unaffected -- both forms have a mutable endpoint. The AUTHORIZED CORRECTION is affected: a lane looking for a literal HEAD to replace will not find one and must ADD a second endpoint instead. SECTION_B6 item 2 states the correction against the measured form.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: At AS_OF_HEAD the synchronized measurement reddens exactly TWO of the four section 6 controls -- N-RC-08 and the exact-write-set control. N-RC-05 and N-RC-06 remain green.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Recorded so no reader infers a blanket section 6 failure. The set that reddens is a function of WHAT integration happens to have changed and will differ at the retry; M1 therefore requires re-derivation and forbids asserting this pair.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: A canary bound to immutable anchors cannot detect a defect introduced into the slice's paths AFTER certification.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Accepted, and compensated rather than denied: SECTION_B10 item 5 gives the present head its own exact-13-path control measured against the integration parent, and SECTION_B7 retains a present-tense untracked arm. Stated here so a future reader does not discover it as a surprise and mistake it for an oversight.

RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.finding: The authorized correction edits a file that is simultaneously one of the certified 13, so a merge commit that also carried the correction would make 'the merge preserved the certified blob' and 'the merge changed it' claims about the same commit.
RISKS_AND_OPEN_FINDINGS.impact: Mitigated by SECTION_B9's requirement that the correction's topology and ordering be explicit and independently certified. Not eliminated -- it depends on the retry lane honouring that clause.
